page: Microsoft Azure FX64-32mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1344.0 GB of RAM, yielding 42.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core execution, image processing, and text processing, all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds are strong, placing in the top 25% with 241.54 GB/sec and 136.66 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also show strong performance. However, database operations and Redis SET operations perform in the average tier. While the server handles prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models efficiently, text generation for large 70B models is weak, registering at 2.71 tokens/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated Intel Xeon hardware, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The inclusion of 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides a high-density resource profile for large-scale caching and in-memory databases. The server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale data decompression, text and image processing pipelines, and medium-scale language model prompt processing.
